Book helpers

Source: vignettes/book-helpers.qmd

The chapters in ggplot2: field manual use a few small helpers for callout boxes and filtering. This vignette covers what each one returns and how to use it in a Quarto chunk.

library(fmggp2)

Callout boxes

co_box() and status() print the markdown for a Quarto callout. They return nothing; the markdown is the side effect. That means you’ll need results: asis in the chunk options, otherwise Quarto shows the raw markdown instead of the callout.

co_box()

The color argument picks the callout type: "b" (note), "g" (tip), "r" (important), "o" (warning), or "y" (caution).

co_box(color = "b", header = "Note", contents = "Simulated data is reproducible with `set.seed()`.")
#> 
#> 
#> :::: {.callout-note collapse='false' appearance='default'}
#> 
#> ## [Note]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.10em;'}
#> 
#> ::: {style='font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;'}
#> 
#> 
#> Simulated data is reproducible with `set.seed()`.
#> 
#> ::: 
#> 
#> ::::

With results: asis, the same call renders as a callout:

Note

Simulated data is reproducible with set.seed().

Set fold = TRUE to collapse the callout and look to "simple" or "minimal" to change its appearance.

status()

status() marks how complete a chapter is. The type argument is one of "polish", "dev", "draft", or "complete".

status("complete")

Tip

This graph is largely complete and just needs final proof reading.

Not in

%nin% is the negation of %in%. I’ve found it reads more naturally than !(x %in% y) inside dplyr::filter().

c("AOL", "Napster", "Netscape") %nin% c("Napster")
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE
